## Proof

Let $(E, p)$ be an elliptic curve, i.e., a genus 1 curve equipped with a distinguished $k$-rational point $p$ serving as the origin. We establish the canonical bijection

$$\Phi : E(k) \;\longrightarrow\; \operatorname{Pic}^{0}(E), \qquad q \;\longmapsto\; \mathcal{O}_{E}\bigl([q]-[p]\bigr),$$

between the set of degree 1 points of $E$ (the $k$-rational points, each yielding a degree 1 divisor $[q]$) and the set of degree 0 invertible sheaves $\operatorname{Pic}^{0}(E)$.

---

### Injectivity

Suppose $\Phi(q) = \Phi(q')$, i.e., $\mathcal{O}_{E}([q]-[p]) \cong \mathcal{O}_{E}([q']-[p])$. Then the divisors $[q]-[p]$ and $[q']-[p]$ are linearly equivalent, so $[q] \sim [q']$. This means there exists a rational function $f \in k(E)^{\times}$ with $\operatorname{div}(f) = [q] - [q']$.

If $q \neq q'$, then $f$ is a non-constant rational function of degree 1 (its divisor has a single zero of order 1 and a single pole of order 1). But a non-constant morphism $f : E \to \mathbb{P}^{1}$ of degree 1 would be an isomorphism, which is impossible since $E$ has genus 1 and $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ has genus 0. Equivalently, by Riemann–Roch on a genus 1 curve, $\ell([q]) = h^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{E}([q])) = 1$ (only the constant functions), so there is no non-constant function with a single simple pole. Hence $q = q'$.

---

### Surjectivity

Let $L$ be any degree 0 invertible sheaf on $E$. Consider the twisted sheaf $L([p]) = L \otimes \mathcal{O}_{E}([p])$, which has degree $\deg L + 1 = 1$.

By the Riemann–Roch theorem for a genus 1 curve ($g = 1$, so $2g - 2 = 0$): for any divisor $D$ with $\deg D > 0$,

$$\ell(D) = h^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{E}(D)) = \deg D.$$

Since $\deg(L([p])) = 1 > 0$, we get $h^{0}(L([p])) = 1$. Therefore $L([p])$ admits a nonzero global section $s$. This section determines an effective divisor $[q]$ of degree 1 (a single $k$-rational point $q$) such that

$$L([p]) \;\cong\; \mathcal{O}_{E}([q]).$$

Tensoring both sides with $\mathcal{O}_{E}(-[p])$ yields

$$L \;\cong\; \mathcal{O}_{E}\bigl([q]-[p]\bigr) = \Phi(q).$$

Thus $\Phi$ is surjective.

---

### Conclusion

The map

$$\boxed{\;\Phi : q \;\longmapsto\; \mathcal{O}_{E}\bigl([q]-[p]\bigr)\;}$$

is a bijection from the set of degree 1 points of $E$ to the set of degree 0 invertible sheaves on $E$. This is the **canonical bijection** determined by the choice of origin $p$: each degree 0 sheaf $L$ corresponds to the unique point $q \in E(k)$ such that $L \cong \mathcal{O}_{E}([q]-[p])$, i.e., the unique effective degree 1 divisor in the linear system $|L([p])|$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
